saints.name: St. Anthony Mary Claret
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A Catalan weaver's son turned tireless missionary, founder of the Claretians and archbishop of Santiago de Cuba…
biography: Born in 1807 at Sallent in Catalonia, the son of a weaver, Anthony Mary Claret was ordained a priest and gave himself to popular missions and to the spread of good books, founding a religious congregation now known as the Claretians. In 1850 he was made Archbishop of Santiago de Cuba, where he reformed the Church and endured attempts on his life.

Recalled to Spain as confessor to Queen Isabella II, he was drawn into the turmoil of court and revolution and followed the queen into exile. A man of ceaseless preaching, writing, and prayer, he died in exile in France in 1870 and was canonized in 1950.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Claretians and his tireless preaching.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Anthony Mary Claret (vatican.va)
